dateline: Hawthorne, CA / Boca Chica, TX — May 2002–Present
heroHeadline: June 5: Crew Dragon Shields ISS Crew from Air Leak — Roadshow Live; 70 Launches in 2026; 621 Total Landings
heroSubtitle: 8,796 days since SpaceX founding — the SpaceX IPO roadshow officially launched June 4–8 at $135/share (555.56M Class A shares, ~$75B raise, $1.77T implied valuation) as CFO Brett Johnson released a 17-minute retail investor video targeting 70% gross margins and 45% net profit margins. On June 5, NASA ordered four Crew-12 astronauts and one crewmember to don suits and shelter aboard the docked SpaceX Crew Dragon after a worsening air leak in the Zvezda service module's transfer tunnel reached ~1 kg/day — the crew returned to the station after Roscosmos chose pressure measurements over immediate repairs. The week also saw SpaceX's 69th (Starlink 17-47, June 3, Vandenberg SLC-4E, OCISLY 620th landing) and 70th (Starlink 10-43, June 4, SLC-40 Cape Canaveral, B1090 12th flight, ASOG 153rd/621st landing) orbital missions of 2026, delivering 53 satellites within 19 hours across two coasts. Morningstar values SpaceX at ~$780B (55% below ask); New Constructs projects $1.1T annual revenue by 2035 required to justify the price. Starship remains FAA-grounded pending IFT-12 mishap investigation resolution; IFT-13 (Booster 20 + Ship 40) targets July–August 2026. IPO pricing June 11; Nasdaq (SPCX) debut June 12.
